uncited: - Estimated camera poses for training images ($P_{train}$) and ground truth poses for training images ($P_{train}^{gt}$).
- Estimated camera poses for test images ($P_{test}$).
- Photometric loss function ($\mathcal{L}_{photo}$) and a NeRF model (or similar implicit representation).
- Optimized camera poses for test images ($P_{test}^{opt}$).
- Camera pose $P_i$ represented as a $4 \times 4$ transformation matrix or a tuple $(R_i, t_i)$ where $R_i \in SO(3)$ and $t_i \in \mathbb{R}^3$.
**Sim(3) Initialization:** Compute a Sim(3) transformation matrix $T_{sim3}$ using Procrustes analysis on the camera pose locations (centers) of the training images.
**Test-time Optimization:** Optimize the parameters of $P_{test}^{init}$ by minimizing the photometric loss $\mathcal{L}_{photo}$ between rendered images and ground truth test images.
A variant using specific initialization schemes for direction vectors.
Fixed initialization sets all initial directions to [Center, Above, Center] (North pole).
When optimizing poses in SO(3), predicted camera locations are overwritten using $t_i = -R_i \times T_i$.
A variant where test-time optimization is interleaved with the training process.
It registers test cameras using the Procrustes transformation from training images and optimizes test poses with photometric loss to factor out pose error effects.
- **Time Complexity:** Depends on the number of optimization iterations and the cost of rendering per iteration.
- **Memory Complexity:** Low, as it only stores pose parameters and the existing NeRF model.
- **When to use:** When global alignment of test poses to training poses is feasible and outliers are minimal.
